HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, MARCH 6, 2024
  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA DR.
  PACIFIC GATEWAY, 3:30 PM

Julie Lie, Chair  Jeffrey Johnson, Member
Desiree Rew, Vice Chair  Doug Killion, Member
Sarah Bedy, Member  Kimberly Lewis, Member
Pam Chotiswatdi, Member  Mary Simmons, Member
James Howat, Member  Susana Sngiem, Member

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Homeless Services Advisory Committee of the City of Long Beach convened
at 3:39 p.m. at Pacific Gateway.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Lie, Rew, Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Johnson, Simmons, Sngiem

Also present: Stephanie Sosa, Community Program Specialist, Jennifer Santana, Secretary,
Jeffrey Proctor, Attendee.

Chair Julie Lie presiding.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  24-52419  Recommendation to approve the Homeless Services Advisory Committee meeting
  minutes from Wednesday, January 10, 2024.

  A motion was made by Howat, seconded by Vice Chair Rew, to approve
  recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Lie, Rew, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Simmons
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Bedy, Sngiem

2.  24-52420  Recommendation to receive and file the Library Services Presentation.

  Cynthia Bautista, Manager of Library Services, Branch Services, presented in
  person.
  • The presentation highlighted the impact of homelessness on library services,
  including challenges such as safety incidents, closures, and the need for

  Page 1 of 5
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, MARCH 6, 2024
  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA DR.
  PACIFIC GATEWAY, 3:30 PM

  additional security.
  • Services offered to the homeless population were also discussed, including
  health educators and outreach teams providing support and guidance to
  individuals experiencing homelessness.
  • Health educators from HSB are located at BJK Main, Mart Twain, and
  Michelle Obama libraries.
  • Library staff need support for dealing with safety issues, including burnout
  and secondary traumatic stress.
  • Members and staff engaged in questions and responses regarding the topics
  presented.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Rew, seconded by Howat, to approve
  recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Lie, Rew, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Simmons
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Bedy, Sngiem

3.  24-52421  Recommendation to receive and file the Subcommittee updates.

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee Update
  • Member Jim Howat provided the update.
  • Project funding increased from $12,000 to $20,000, raising concerns.
  • The council approved a $5,000 grant for GP blankets of love.
  • Concerns were raised about the lack of detailed project proposals and the
  need for timely access to applications for review.
  • City Staff and committee members discussed gap needs and gap funding.
  Policy Subcommittee Update
  • Chair Julie Lie provided the update.
  • The committee continues to meet council members regarding the safe sleep
  project.
  • Members discussed the idea of creating designated parking spaces for RVs
  as a potential solution for individuals living in RVs.
  • Member Sarah Bedy is working on a policy recommendation draft that will be
  shared with the council.
  • There is discussion around a city-wide field trip to Culver City for council
  members to learn more about the Culver City Safe Sleep program.
  Continuum of Care Board Update
  • Member Pam Chotiswatdi provided an update.
  • The CoC is working on governance policy and increasing attendance.
  • There was a Special Meeting on the Homeless Strategic Plan
  • There have been a few Strategic Plan listening sessions for service

  providers and the CoC Board, HSAC will also get to be a part of different
  phases within the next few months.

  A motion was made by Howat, seconded by Member Johnson, to approve
  recommendation. The motion by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Lie, Rew, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Simmons
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Bedy, Sngiem

4.  24-52422  Recommendation to approve the Mayor’s Fund Application for GP Blankets of love
  for $5000.

  Member Jim Howat provided the update.
  • The application was submitted for $20,000, however, the committee agreed
  that $5000 would be the amount granted.
  • The total on application reflects $5,083, but only $5,000 was approved.
  • A representative of GP Blankets of love introduced herself and welcomed
  any questions.

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Rew, seconded by Howat, to approve
  recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Lie, Rew, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Simmons
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Bedy, Sngiem

5.  24-52423  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff Report.

  Jeffrey Proctor, Homeless Services Special Projects Officer presented.
  • Outreach direct phone number, 562-470-4672(4MSC) is live and taking calls.
  o 404 requests for Outreach
  o 274 newly enrolled people in outreach
  o 453 outreach services were provided.
  o 346 first-time visitors to the MSC
  o 3,285 total visits in February
  o 157 average daily visits
  o 1,444 phone calls answered.
  o 137 Mobile Access Enrollments

  o 251 Mobile Access Center Services Provided
  • March MSC & Outreach Numbers
  o Shelter site occupancy
  o Project home key- 1725 Long Beach 88% (85)
  o Atlantic Bridge Community 96% (120)
  o Motel Voucher Program 15 avg.
  o Safe Parking 14 avg.
  o 702 W. Anaheim St. 99% (80)
  o New intakes were paused while working through the transition.
  Intakes have just recently resumed.
  • Operation updates
  o Jennifer Santana has been promoted to Community Program
  Specialist II and will continue to support HSAC and the Mayor's Fund.
  o Construction has begun for the Luxury Inn PHK site 5950 Long Beach
  Blvd. There will be a press conference event later in March.
  o The City has assumed operational oversight of PHK Best Western.
  o The inclement weather shelter at the MSC was activated for 20 days
  during February with an average of 58 people.
  o The city has begun hosting listening sessions with City Fabrik to get
  input for the homelessness strategic plan.
  o The city will be partnering with the County on another Pathway Home
  project.
  o The city is close to a deal with a motel lease for the encampment
  resolutions project focused on the downtown area.
  o Members of the public asked about safe parking vehicle distribution
  and motel voucher capacity.
  o City staff responded.

  A motion was made by Howat, seconded by Vice Chair Rew, to approve

  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Bedy, Sngiem
